I will do it much like last year, with a few small changes if the price of fertilizer is too high. I have 12 mu, and in my place the land does not rest, so the wheat is on 12 mu and after that the maize is also on the same 12 mu. I do not like taking chances with yield. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose grain, that loss is bigger than the money I saved. So I will still put enough base fertilizer on the land, and I will follow what the better farmers around me do. For wheat, I will use an improved seed because the old local seed does not give as much grain now. I will water it about 3 times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at filling. I will feed wheat a bit heavier because wheat needs a steady stand through winter and spring. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here the hybrids give fuller ears and more grain, and I have seen that myself on other people’s fields. Maize grows fast, so I will give it strong fertilizer too, mostly nitrogen, and I will water it about 2 times with the well if rain is not enough. Wheat I will spray about 2 times, mainly for weeds and then for disease or aphids if they come. Maize I will also spray about 2 times, once for weeds early and once for insects later. For wheat I will use rotary tillage after maize harvest because that is what I am used to and it leaves a decent seedbed. For maize, because wheat harvest and maize sowing are tight together, I will do no-tillage on the wheat stubble if I can get it done quickly. That saves time and catches moisture.
